{
  "success_memory_items": [
    {
      "title": "Write a temporary self-test harness before/after implementing",
      "pattern": "After reading the stub and package config, create a throwaway test script (e.g. selftest.mjs) that imports the module under test and asserts expected outputs, run it with node, then delete it before finishing. The harness encodes the spec's own examples plus edge cases.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden grader cannot be inspected, so a local harness is the only feedback loop. It converts the prose spec into executable checks, catching wrong assumptions (e.g. grouping, casing, error behavior) before submission.",
      "examples": [
        "cat > selftest.mjs with cases like encode('test',{a:5,b:7})==='ybty' then `node selftest.mjs`",
        "selftest.mjs asserting recite(10,10) full song and recite(10,1) single verse, then `rm -f selftest.mjs`"
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises with hidden tests",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Build an independent reference implementation for differential testing",
      "pattern": "For algorithmic tasks, write a second, deliberately different implementation (brute force, exhaustive enumeration, or direct formula) and compare its output against the primary implementation across many generated inputs.",
      "why_it_helps": "Two independent derivations agreeing is strong evidence of correctness and catches subtle bugs (modular inverse, tie-breaking, boundary handling) that a hand-written example set would miss.",
      "examples": [
        "gen.mjs brute-forcing the modular inverse over a in 1..25 and comparing against encode/decode for many keys",
        "verify2.tmp.mjs enumerating all reachable tic-tac-toe boards by legal play and comparing to gamestate()",
        "brute-force agreement over 460 cases for killer-sudoku combinations"
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks with a well-defined mathematical or combinatorial spec",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Derive expected values from the spec text, not from the implementation",
      "pattern": "When writing self-tests, transcribe expected outputs verbatim from the problem statement (examples, tables, sample lyrics) rather than from what the code currently produces.",
      "why_it_helps": "Prevents the self-test from simply mirroring a buggy implementation; it anchors correctness to the authoritative spec, which is what the hidden grader encodes.",
      "examples": [
        "space-age self-test using the spec's 31.69 Earth-years and planet orbital periods",
        "bottle-song test embedding the full 10-verse lyric from the instructions",
        "tournament test using the exact header string and example table from the spec"
      ],
      "scope": "Any spec-driven exercise",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Explicitly test boundary and degenerate inputs",
      "pattern": "Include cases for empty input, zero, negative, out-of-range, non-coprime keys, wrong-size grids, single-element ranges, and 'no valid combination' scenarios in the self-test.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders typically include these edge cases; exercising them locally surfaces off-by-one and validation-order bugs (e.g. which error to throw first).",
      "examples": [
        "affine-cipher tests for a=0 / non-coprime a throwing, and digits passing through unchanged",
        "triangle tests for degenerate 1,1,2 and 1,2,3 with the >= inequality",
        "ocr-numbers tests for wrong width and garbled glyphs returning '?'"
      ],
      "scope": "All exercises with validation or boundary rules",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Verify module contract: exports, syntax, and no leftover stub throws",
      "pattern": "Before finishing, run `node --check <file>` and a small import that prints exported keys and a sample call; also grep for the stub's 'Remove this statement' throw to confirm it was replaced.",
      "why_it_helps": "Catches syntax errors, wrong export names/shapes, and accidentally retained stub code that would fail every hidden test regardless of logic.",
      "examples": [
        "node --check affine-cipher.js && node -e \"import('./affine-cipher.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m)))\"",
        "grep -n \"Remove this statement\" bottle-song.js || echo \"no stub throw left\""
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises",
      "confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up temporary artifacts before finishing",
      "pattern": "Delete all scratch test/reference files (selftest.mjs, gen.mjs, verify*.mjs, temp copies) and confirm the directory contains only the intended solution file plus original config.",
      "why_it_helps": "Avoids leaving stray files that could confuse the grader or violate the 'do not create test files' constraint, and confirms the final workspace state.",
      "examples": [
        "rm -f selftest.mjs gen.mjs && node --check affine-cipher.js && ls -a",
        "rm -f selftest.tmp.mjs verify.tmp.mjs verify2.tmp.mjs && ls -la"
      ],
      "scope": "All exercises",
      "confidence": 0.75
    },
    {
      "title": "Isolate the failing case with a minimal diagnostic script",
      "pattern": "When a self-test fails, write a tiny one-off script that prints the actual intermediate values (character codes, counts, slices) for the specific failing input instead of guessing.",
      "why_it_helps": "Turns a vague mismatch into concrete data (e.g. revealing a wrong slice index or an unexpected character), enabling a targeted fix rather than blind edits.",
      "examples": [
        "node -e printing charCodeAt for each cell to debug tic-tac-toe board parsing",
        "node -e printing line lengths of an OCR grid to find the off-by-one column split"
      ],
      "scope": "Debugging any failing self-test",
      "confidence": 0.8
    },
    {
      "title": "Preserve input immutability and stable ordering",
      "pattern": "When the spec implies sorting or aggregation, copy the input before sorting and use a deterministic tie-break (e.g. alphabetical) so repeated calls are stable and the caller's array is not mutated.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden tests often check that inputs are unchanged and that ties resolve deterministically; mutating the caller's array or unstable sorts cause intermittent failures.",
      "examples": [
        "ledger self-test 'input array not mutated' and tie-break by description",
        "tournament sorting by points desc then team name asc"
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks involving sorting/aggregation of caller-provided data",
      "confidence": 0.7
    }
  ]
}
